annotation.title_clean: Implementing International Humanitarian Law in the Use of Autonomy in Weapon Systems
annotation.title_en: Implementing International Humanitarian Law in the Use of Autonomy in Weapon Systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States of America (submission to CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS, CCW/GGE.1/2019/WP.5
named_instruments_referenced: CCW Protocol V on Explosive Remnants of War
annotation.summary_en: US working paper to the 2019 CCW GGE on lethal autonomous weapons systems. It argues that existing international humanitarian law (distinction, proportionality, precaution) already provides a comprehensive framework for autonomy in weapons. Its main points are that legal weapons reviews, testing and doctrine are key ways of applying IHL, and that autonomous functions can strengthen compliance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Existing IHL provides a comprehensive framework to govern autonomy in weapon systems
IHL duties fall on combatants and commands, not machines
Rigorous testing, doctrine/training/procedures and legal weapons reviews are essential to IHL compliance
Three scenarios of autonomous function use analysed for distinction, proportionality, precaution
LAWS technologies could reduce civilian casualties, log operations for accountability, flag incidents and track unexploded ordnance
